audits.title: Auditing health care providers’ infection control related practices in hemodialysis units in Menoufia Governorate in Egypt
audits.standard: CDC-recommended infection prevention practices in haemodialysis

audits.title: The Infection Prevention and Biosafety Assessment Initiative: Impact of a Structured Multimodal Training Intervention on Infection Prevention and Biosafety Compliance in a Resource-Limited Setting
audits.standard: IPBAI tool of ten domains aligned with WHO IPC core components
audits.setting: Nine clinical departments, tertiary cardiac care centre, Karachi

cycle1.result: General indicator score 72.5%; standard and transmission-based precautions 20%; environmental cleaning 0%; spill response 20%; antimicrobial stewardship 20%.

audits.intervention: Structured multimodal IPC training module delivered in two cycles to 607 healthcare workers.

cycle2.result: General indicator score 94%; all ten domains 100%.

audits.other_findings: Training reached 391 staff in the first cycle and 216 in the second.
audits.citation: Khan MA, Basheer V, Palous M, Sheraz N, Khan SA, Hanif B. The Infection Prevention and Biosafety Assessment Initiative: Impact of a Structured Multimodal Training Intervention on Infection Prevention and Biosafety Compliance in a Resource-Limited Setting. . 2026. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10453026/v1.

audits.title: Waterbirths: regional audit of infection control practices.
audits.setting: 16 maternity centres in a region (questionnaire to infection control nurses)

cycle1.result: 14 (88%) centres responded, 11 did waterbirths; all 8 with on-site pools had infection control policies; 6 used detergent and disinfectant, 2 detergent alone; no centre tested mothers for blood-borne viruses; 2 did regular microbiological testing of pools

audits.other_findings: Six centres collected infection data on mother or child. Authors recommend policies covering pool decontamination, legionella prevention and PPE.
audits.citation: Kingsley A, Hutter S, Green N, Speirs G. Waterbirths: regional audit of infection control practices. J Hosp Infect. 1999;41(2):155-157. doi:10.1016/s0195-6701(99)90054-3. PMID: 10063479.

audits.title: Nursing homes infection control audit.
audits.standard: Recommendations: trained infection control link nurse, reference material, response to enteric outbreaks, MRSA/C. diff recording, influenza vaccination
audits.setting: All 23 nursing homes in Forth Valley Health Board area (telephone audit)

cycle1.result: 17 (74%) had link nurses; 11% attended PHICN induction; specimens taken 33%; notes flagged 73%; none informed Public Health of outbreaks.

cycle2.result: 19 (83%) had link nurses; 16% attended induction; specimens taken 88%; notes flagged 100%; one informed Public Health.

audits.other_findings: Reference material availability remained a concern; MRSA carriers recorded 75% vs 83%.
audits.citation: Holliday AJ, Murdoch S. Nursing homes infection control audit. Health Bull (Edinb). 2001;59(6):356-363. PMID: 12661385.

audits.title: The procedures of hygiene to control hospital-acquired diarrhoea in paediatric wards: a multicentre audit.
audits.standard: Recommended hygiene procedures for control of hospital-acquired diarrhoea

cycle1.result: Handwashing before care in over 95% of procedures; glove use 39.4% for technical procedures and 20.3% for diapering or temperature measurement.

audits.other_findings: Agreement between reported and observed hygiene was only moderate for single rooms, handwashing after contact, overclothing and gloves after diaper change.

audits.title: Steady improvement of infection control services in six community hospitals in Makkah following annual audits during Hajj for four consecutive years.
audits.setting: Six Ministry of Health community hospitals, Makkah, during Hajj

cycle1.result: Average score across 11 infection control items 43% (range 20-67%); lacked committees, units, education, surveillance and staff.

audits.title: Infection control audit and potential sources of infection of a Nigerian eye unit.
audits.standard: Infection control procedures and practices (pre-designed questionnaire)
audits.setting: Eye clinic and theatre, Lagos University Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: No post-operative infections in 207 procedures; deficiencies in hand drying and washing, steriliser training, undated packs, waste segregation and equipment disinfection.

audits.other_findings: Potential infection sources included staff nares, surgical packs, theatre bed, surgeons' hands and patient conjunctivae.

audits.title: Improving Adherence to Infection Prevention and Disinfection Protocols Within the Ophthalmology Department: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project (QIP).
audits.standard: Hospital infection control standards in line with MOH and CBAHI frameworks; aim >90% compliance across all domains
audits.setting: Multispecialty ophthalmology clinics, Magrabi Hospital, Riyadh

cycle1.result: Staff self-report survey: aware of disinfection policy 87.5%; annual training 45.8%; staff wear masks 39.6%; disinfection logs maintained 75.0%; multidose drops used for one patient only 58.3%; high-touch surfaces cleaned after each patient 66.7%.

audits.intervention: Revised guidelines with visual guides for infection protocols and hand hygiene, emphasis on mask use and log keeping, quality team reminders, online training for all clinical staff and training at induction.

cycle2.result: Aware of policy 93.2%; annual training 63.4%; masks 68.2% (p=0.01); logs maintained 95.4% (p=0.01); multidose drops single-patient use fell to 18.2% (p<0.01); high-touch cleaning 72.7%.

audits.other_findings: Shared cleaning responsibility fell from 75.0% to 54.5% and disposable tonometer tip use stayed at 6.8%; data were self-reported rather than observed.
audits.citation: Bakheet M, Chaudhary A, Al Thubaiti GA, Al Assiri AA. Improving Adherence to Infection Prevention and Disinfection Protocols Within the Ophthalmology Department: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project (QIP). Cureus. 2026;18(5):e109333. doi:10.7759/cureus.109333. PMID: 42326150.

audits.title: The effects of trained observers (dofficers) and audits during a facility-wide COVID-19 outbreak: A mixed-methods quality improvement analysis.
audits.standard: 21-point audit of infection control bundle (signage, equipment, PPE use, environmental cleaning, cohorting and social distancing)
audits.setting: Tertiary acute care hospital during a facility-wide COVID-19 outbreak
audits.intervention: Trained observers (dofficers, furloughed staff) giving real-time corrective feedback on PPE use, and weekly quality improvement reports to units.
audits.other_findings: 962 audits recorded 36,948 observations; most common errors were environmental cleaning and PPE use, and error rates remained high.
audits.citation: Picard C, Edlund M, Keddie C, Asadi L, O'Dochartaigh D, Drew R, et al.. The effects of trained observers (dofficers) and audits during a facility-wide COVID-19 outbreak: A mixed-methods quality improvement analysis. Am J Infect Control. 2021;49(9):1136-1141. doi:10.1016/j.ajic.2021.03.011. PMID: 33774100.
